card.name: Gavotte
card.era: Attested 16th c.; court favorite under Louis XIV; Breton folk form attested late 18th c.
card.tagline: French dance - both a Breton folk dance and a Baroque court dance.
card.profile: The gavotte is a French dance in 4/4 or 2/2 of moderate tempo, taking its name from the Gavot people of the Pays de Gap (Dauphine), per one tradition; another holds the name is generic, most likely originating in Lower Brittany (Wikipedia). As a Renaissance/Baroque dance it derived from the double branle, became popular at the court of Louis XIV (Lully, Rameau, Bach), and sits among the optional galanteries of the suite, typically with a half-bar upbeat. The Breton gavotte (gavotte bretonne / dans tro) is a major family of chain and round dances of Lower Brittany with many terroir variants - gavotte de l'Aven, gavotte des montagnes, dans fisel, gavotte glazik - danced in fest-noz to biniou-and-bombarde or kan-ha-diskan singing (Wikipedia; Wikipedia FR).
card.insight: French scholarship notes the Breton 'gavotte' label is a misnomer applied by outsiders: the Breton dans tro probably descends from 16th-c. trihoris rather than the French Renaissance branles, so the courtly gavotte and the Breton dance are largely unrelated traditions sharing a borrowed name (Wikipedia FR, Dans tro).
card.image_significance: Brittany's most widespread chain dance. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Brittany, France.
